entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Raphia is a pivotal event in the history of the Ptolemaic Kingdom, marking a decisive victory for Ptolemy V over the Seleucid Empire. Occurring in 217 BCE, this battle had far-reaching consequences for the balance of power in the ancient Mediterranean world.

The Battle of Raphia took place in the Gaza region of southern Palestine, a strategic location that controlled access to the important trade routes between Egypt and the Levant. The Ptolemaic Kingdom, under the leadership of Ptolemy V, sought to assert its dominance over the Seleucid Empire, which had been expanding its territories in the region.

The battle was a turning point in the history of the Ptolemaic Kingdom, as Ptolemy V emerged victorious, securing a significant advantage over the Seleucid Empire. This victory had lasting impacts on the politics and trade of the ancient Mediterranean world, shaping the course of history for centuries to come.

As the dust settled, the Battle of Raphia left an indelible mark on the region, influencing the rise and fall of empires and civilizations for generations to come.
